plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads made of golden ray petals surrounding a dark central disk. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky, and the plant is widely grown for seed, oil and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; widely cultivated across the United States, Europe, Ukraine, Russia and Argentina
plants.funFact: Young sunflower buds follow the sun from east to west in a behavior called heliotropism, but mature blooms generally stay facing east.

plants.name: Solidago canadensis
plants.description: A perennial wildflower forming tall stems topped with plumes of tiny golden flower heads. It thrives in meadows, roadsides and open fields, and provides late-season nectar for bees, butterflies and other pollinators.
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; naturalized in Europe and Asia
plants.funFact: Goldenrod is often blamed for hay fever, but the real culprit is usually ragweed, which blooms at the same time; goldenrod pollen is heavy and spread by insects.

plants.name: Eucalyptus leucoxylon
plants.description: A medium-sized Australian tree with smooth mottled bark and clusters of fluffy stamens in place of petals. It flowers heavily in the Southern Hemisphere's late winter and early spring, attracting honeyeaters and lorikeets.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (May to October, peaking around August to September)
plants.location: South Australia, Victoria and New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: Yellow Gum is a key nectar source for native birds and the honey industry, and its flower color varies from white and cream to deep red among individual trees.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulbous perennial that sends up crocus-like lilac-pink flowers in late summer and early autumn, before its leaves appear in spring. The flowers emerge directly from the ground on bare stems.
plants.location: Native to Europe, in damp meadows and woodland edges; cultivated in gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: All parts of the plant contain colchicine, a toxic compound that is also used in medicine to treat gout and in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.
